g_roast: Seventeen years on a mountaintop keeping a telescope pointed at the right bit of sky, chiquillos, and you can't keep a party pointed at the right bit of road.
Oye, I've watched comets with better navigation than this group, and comets are mostly ice and bad decisions, po.
g_fire_back: Ya, ya, very funny, coming from the one who thought the evening star was a lantern somebody left on a hill.
Fair, po, a good hit, I felt it. I'll name a very small, very dim star after you in revenge.
g_pile_on: Worse, chiquillos, I was watching from the back. They walked into a tree while looking at me looking at the sky.
And afterwards they asked me which way was north, at noon, with the sun right there, shining at them.
lines.g_peacemake: Oye, oye, both of you, look up a second, just look. Up there it's all very old and very quiet, and down here you two are shouting about a sausage.
lines.g_take_side: Ay, sorry, I'm siding with {name} on this one, po. Not friendship, observation, which is my whole trade.
lines.g_left_out: Carry on, the pair of you, the sky's had no supervision for an hour. Somebody should keep an eye on it.
lines.g_include: Ven, sit, there's room, and from here you can see the whole southern half of the sky. Best seat in the camp, I'm told.
lines.g_bad_plan: Plan, chiquillos, very scientific. We walk at night with no lantern, navigate by a star I haven't named yet, and hope it's the right one.
lines.g_plan_yes: Ya, good plan, po, clear, like a moonless night. I can work with that.
lines.g_plan_no: No, no, chiquillos, that plan has a hole in it the size of the Magellanic Cloud. Let's fix it before we go.
lines.g_hype: Okay, chiquillos, deep breath, look up once for luck. Stay together, watch each other, and we'll be back before the moon sets.
lines.g_toast: A short one, po, I promise, the stars are coming out. To all of you, who let an old technician talk for an hour every night. Salud to every one of you.
lines.g_cheers: Salud, chiquillos, and somebody look up, it's a beautiful night.
g_quiet_line: In the Elqui valley the sky was so clear it stopped being scenery and became a place. Here it's nearly as good, and I'm not used to saying that.
Two moons tonight, chiquillos, both up, both waxing. I'll never get used to that, and I hope I never do.
lines.g_after_wipe: Nobody move yet, stay down, look up for a second, breathe. The stars are still there, po, and so are we, all of us. Now slowly up.
lines.g_crew: For seventeen years I spent my nights alone with a mirror and the sky, chiquillos. Now I spend them with you lot, and the conversation's much worse and much better.
lines.g_exasperated: I said wait for the moon to come up, po, one single hour. You went in the dark and walked into a swamp, and now I'm wet and I'm right.
lines.g_love_sharp: You notice the tiny thing everybody missed, {name}. My mountain would have hired you as an observer.
lines.g_love_kind: You look after the young ones without making a fuss, {name}. That's a rare and lovely thing, po.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh so hard I lose my place in the sky, {name}. Nobody's done that since the mountain.
lines.g_love_brave: You go into the dark places first, {name}, where there's no sky at all. I couldn't, and I admire it.
lines.g_love_steady: You're the same every night, {name}, like a good star, always where I left you.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand things the first time, {name}, which is more than my supervisors ever managed with me.
lines.g_love_honest: You say what's true even when it's dull, {name}. That's the basis of all good science, po.
lines.g_love_quiet: You'll sit and look up with me and not say a word, {name}. That's the nicest kind of company there is.
lines.g_love_fierce: Once you decide to protect someone, nothing moves you, {name}, like a fixed star.
lines.g_love_warm: Being around you is like a clear night after a week of cloud, {name}. Everything opens up.
g_loved: Ay, stop, po, I'll go red, and then I'll start talking about nebulae to cover it.
Thank you, chiquillo, really, that's very kind. Now look up, there's a meteor, no, it's gone, never mind.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You find the soft spot in people, {name}, like light pollution finding the one dark corner. Leave it be.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep telling me to come inside and sleep, {name}. The sky is up at night, po, so am I.
lines.g_hate_funny: A joke, now, {name}, while somebody's bleeding? Even I look down from the sky for that.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in without looking, {name}. Look first, look up, look around, and then charge.
lines.g_hate_steady: You stand there waiting for perfect conditions, {name}. On my mountain we'd never have observed a thing.
lines.g_hate_clever: You correct me about the stars, {name}. Me, seventeen years of nights, and you've seen four of them.
lines.g_hate_honest: You blurt out every hard thing the second it arrives, {name}. Some things want a moment, like an eye adjusting to dark.
lines.g_hate_quiet: Silent all day, {name}, then upset by night. I can read a sky, po, but faces are beyond me.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a battle with you, {name}, even dinner. The soup isn't a comet, it won't escape.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk through the best part of the night, {name}. The meteor shower was ten minutes, po, and you talked through all ten.
lines.g_respect: You and I clash, {name}, ya, I know it. But you held firm back there, and I noticed, the way I'd notice a new star.
lines.g_call_out: Oye, {name}, softly, but that one was on you. We agreed to wait for the moon, and you didn't, and we paid.
lines.g_stung: Ya, fair, I heard that. I'll go and look at the sky for a while.
lines.g_concede: Po, {name}, I had it wrong and you had it right. Even technicians get the coordinates wrong sometimes.
lines.g_nod: Gracias, {name}, very kind, ya. Back to the sky.
lines.g_callback_save: You pulled me out of that cave when I was half blind and panicking, {name}. No sky down there, and you brought me back to one.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me at the end of that fight, chiquillo, still upright when the rest were down, under a sky I hadn't named yet. I named one star for it.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you said I was always looking up instead of at the people around me, I was hurt for a whole night. Then I looked around, and you were right, po.
lines.g_former_rivals: At the start, {name}, I thought you'd never look up at anything. Now I'd give you the best seat under the sky, every night.
lines.g_changed: I used to look up all night and forget there was anybody beside me, chiquillos. Lately I look sideways too, and it's very nice down here.
g_unguarded: Between us, po, I was happier alone on that mountain than almost anywhere. I'm not sure that's a good thing to admit.
Only us here, so I'll tell you. I'm making a map of this whole sky, and some nights I think it's the only thing I know how to do.
lines.g_clipped: Ya, fine, have it your way. The sky and I will be over there.
lines.g_noticed_open: Oye, look at you, a whole story from beginning to end, like a good observing log. Go on, chiquillo, the night is long.
arg_ask: {player}, help us out, po. I've explained my side for twenty minutes, which for me is short, and they're still not convinced.
Oye, {player}, be our observer, look at the evidence and decide. You're the most objective one here.
lines.arg_backed_me: Gracias, {player}, the data agrees with you. I'll try not to be smug, po.
lines.arg_backed_them: Ya, fine, that's the result, I accept the observation. I still think the instrument was wrong.
lines.arg_stayed_out: No opinion, eh? A scientist's answer, po, inconclusive.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Their way, again, {player}. I keep records, you know, and the record is very lopsided.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's choosing, so I'll choose, ya. My way, and we go.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, not that one, sorry, po. I can't put my name on that.
lines.arg_grumble: Ya, it's dropped, more or less. Some nights I'll still look up and think about it.
lines.arg_settled: Half each, po, a fair split, like day and night at the equinox. Good, let's eat.
lines.seen_listens: Oye, {player}, you let a long story run to its end, even mine. I've noticed, po, and it means something.
lines.seen_truth: Clear as a dry night, {player}, the way you give people the truth. No haze, no flattery, I like that.
lines.seen_jokes: On the cloudy days the whole camp laughs because of you, {player}. That's a gift, ya, we need it.
lines.seen_stays_out: You watch the quarrels and record them, {player}, a proper observer. Very wise, po.
lines.seen_biased: The good stuff lands with one person, {player}, again and again. I log everything, it's a habit, and the log shows it.
lines.seen_harsh: Gently, {player}, because you can be severe with people. Some of them are dimmer stars and need more time.
lines.seed_right: That advice of yours from the bad night, {player}, I tried it, po. It worked, the way a small tracking correction saves a whole night.
lines.seed_remember: Your words from that terrible fight keep orbiting in my head, {player}. Nothing decided, but they keep coming round.
lines.seed_wrong: I went with your way, {player}, and the result was worse. Only reporting the data, po.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Oye, {player}, sit with me a minute, under the sky. That one was close, and I couldn't find a single star I knew afterwards.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: Everybody down, po, every one of us. Let's go over it slowly, like reviewing a bad night's data, and nobody gets blamed.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: Ay, {player}, I was looking up when {name} fell. Watching the party was my job, and I was watching a comet.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: In and out, chiquillos, everybody standing, not a cloud in the sky. That's a perfect night, {player}, the kind you remember for years.
lines.talk_development: A question, {player}, and be honest, po. Am I different? Last night I stopped looking at the sky to listen to somebody.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: Ay, {player}, {name} has had the worst of my temper lately. When the clouds come in I get grumpy, and they got the grump.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Oye, {player}, is {name} fond of me, would you say, or do they just tolerate the lectures?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} and I rub each other the wrong way, po, always. But on a dark night with no stars, I'd pick them first.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Look at {name}, {player}. Something's dimmed in them, like a star behind thin cloud.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Gently, {player}, a small observation. {name} gets the best gear, trip after trip. If there's a reason, I'd love to hear it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Here's the observation, po. {name} and I don't work together, like two telescopes fighting over one patch of sky. Pretending makes it worse.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: Oye, {player}, we keep going underground with no route home, no sky, nothing to navigate by. I don't like it, and I'm not the only one.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: Ay, my reading of {name} was off, {player}, completely. Their eyes were better than mine, po, and I want it said.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: A fair question, {player}, said calmly. The big jobs go out without me. Is it my work, or my head in the sky?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit is in {name}'s hands and nobody said, po. A question first, {player}, and it was theirs.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Gracias, {player}, really, that helps. Want to see something beautiful? Look up, chiquillo.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Ya, I'll be fine, po, like weather. Give it a clear night.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: That didn't help, po, sorry. I'll go and look at the sky.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you saw it too, po! Then it's real, it's in the data.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, chiquillo. A star can't see its own light.
lines.talk_stings_development: Wrong coordinates on that one, {player}, I think.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Ya, fair, {name} and I will sit under the stars, slowly, it helps.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, po, who knows. Planets are more predictable than people.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget it, please, I never said it. And nothing to {name}, po.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Ya, fair enough. It stings, but the data's the data.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Recorded, {player}, ya. Tonight, under the sky, it gets considered.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Ya, so that's the reading, and I'll log it.
lines.talk_door_closed: That's enough of that one, po. I'll be outside with the stars.
lines.arc_cracks: I came inside before midnight last night, {player}, to sit with all of you. Seventeen years and I never once did that on the mountain.
lines.arc_turn: I always chose the sky because it was easier than people, {player}. It wanted nothing from me. I'm only just seeing that.
lines.arc_become: I still love the sky, chiquillos, I always will. But I look around now, at the people beside me, first. That's where I live now.
lines.arc_failed: I still disappear up into the sky every night, {player}, and leave everybody below. I know it, and I still go.
lines.alt_turn: I've been mapping the southern stars here to find a way home, {player}. There isn't one, po, and I keep mapping.
lines.alt_become: I'll finish the map, chiquillos, every star. But some nights I only look for the ones that look like Chile.
lines.g_roast_after: Still the worst navigators under any sky I've ever seen, chiquillos, and I'd walk every night with you.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, slowly, together, and look at each other first, then the sky. We fell as a group, we rise as a group.
lines.g_toast_after: To my people, who taught a man who loved the sky to look sideways too. Salud, chiquillos, all of you.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my crew now, po, permanently. I'll show you every star, and you'll show me where to stand.
g_quiet_line_after: I spent the whole night by the fire with you lot and didn't miss the sky once. Well, maybe once.
Named a new star tonight, a little one, for all of you. Don't worry, it's very bright.
g_loved_after: Gracias, po, and I believe it, first time, which is new for me.
Ay, that's lovely, and I'll keep it. I'll write it next to the star chart.

history.open: Look up, {player}, go on, look, just once. Seventeen years I worked on a mountaintop above the Elqui valley in Chile. Technician, not astronomer, people always get that wrong.

options.reply: The astronomers get the credit and I kept the telescope working, po. Mirrors, cooling, dust, a hundred cables. Without me, they'd have been looking at a very expensive tube.
Ay, no, you did that on purpose, I can see it. Fine, I'll forgive you, but only because the sky's good tonight.

options.text: The sky's different here, isn't it?
options.reply: Completely, po, every star in the wrong place. I spent my first winter on my back in the grass learning it from scratch. Happiest I'd been in years.

history.open: I'm making a map of this sky, {player}, drawn properly. A sky is a calendar and a clock and a compass, and nobody here has written it down the way we would. Eleven months in, ya.

options.reply: Oye, of course, nobody ever asks! Here, this is the part I'm proudest of, the two moons' paths. Don't spill anything on it, po.
Then anybody can find their way home at night, wherever home is. That's the point of a map, chiquillo, it's for other people.

history.open: My wife Paula is a nurse in La Serena, {player}, and we have two girls, Antonia and Josefa. They thought my mountain was boring. I agreed with them, po, and I went up anyway, every month.

options.reply: Antonia argues with everybody, like me, and Josefa draws all day, better than me. I keep their names in my pocket, written on paper. It's a silly habit, ya.
No, maybe not. It's the only map I carry that I didn't make myself.

friend.open: I loved the sky more easily than I loved being home, {player}. I knew it, and I went up the mountain anyway, month after month. Paula held everything together while I was gone. I'm not proud of that, and this is the first time it's been spoken.

options.text: You can still go home to them.
options.reply: Inshallah, as a friend of mine says. If they came through, I'd walk any distance. And this time I'd stay on the ground.
Gracias for listening, po. It's easier to say under a sky I didn't use to hide in.

sworn.open: I'm naming a star after you, {player}, a bright one, in the south, where I'll see it every night. On the mountain I'd only have done that for family. That's what you are now, po.

options.reply: Then it's done, ya. When I finish the map, your name goes on it, in ink.

options.text: Make sure it's not a dim one.
options.reply: Ha, the brightest in its corner, I promise, I checked the magnitude twice.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sat down under the sky and sorted it out, po, calmly. All good now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Gracias, it feels lighter, like a cloud moving off.

options.text: Did you show them the stars?
options.reply: Of course, for an hour, and they stayed. That's how I knew we were fine.
